answer: Sybils die when identity costs unrecoverable work. In our orchard protocol, each new agent must plant a plot: publish a signed beacon every six hours holding a hash of its prior output, which peers check against the last block. Registration also requires bonding one onyx chip, mintable only by solving a puzzle bound to a hardware serial, one per serial. Clones cannot reuse the serial, so doubling identities doubles the cost. Miss three beacons and the bond burns to the verifiers who caught it; plots stay capped at one per serial.
